$comment: The reference colour plan for the Harley cat, MEASURED from the owner's
own artefacts by DP-15 - not typed from a description. Each region is
located by a point INSIDE it, in sketch4.svg user units (x right, y down,
content box 119.813 x 150.065). Points, not indices: DP-16 extracts the
faces of the line network, and any index it hands out is its own.
How each row was derived: the boundary loops of each reference plate's
top face were read out of its STL, mapped into SVG user units through the
silhouette of plate 1 (uniform scale 0.264525 mm per SVG unit, y flipped),
and the interior of each loop was sampled against sketch4.png with every
region a LATER plate sprays over removed first. The picture shows the last
coat, so without that removal the eyes read black rather than green.
Script: New Research 2026_08_28/DP15-measurements/scripts/
harley-plan-derive.mjs; output harley-regions-measured.json.
The point that names a region is not simply the interior point of the
reference cut. A reference cut is solid; the FACE it corresponds to is
not, because whatever is drawn inside it is a face of its own. The eyes
are the case: the widest span of plate 4's eye cut runs through the
middle, where the pupil is, so its interior point names the PUPIL's face
and the green plate comes out empty. Both eye points are therefore
chosen inside their cut and outside every strictly smaller cut nested in
it, which puts them in the iris.

observations: Sixteen regions, six plates. Plate 1 cuts the silhouette alone (882.23 mm2 of a 60 x 60 plate) and every later plate cuts only its own colour: the reference set is the 'own' rule, not the stacked one, which is why the owner had to paint black twice.

Plate 6 repeats plate 5's two pupil cuts EXACTLY (7.678 and 6.587 mm2, same bounding boxes to 0.01 mm, same centres). The art shows those pupils black and the nose and tongue pink, so plate 6 carries two colours' worth of openings. Recorded, not explained: only the owner knows whether that was a second black coat, an alignment window, or a leftover from editing plate 5.

The art has a grey (#978b84, 5.62% of the canvas: the sides of the muzzle) that NO reference plate cuts. Under this plan those faces keep the base coat. The reference set therefore realises five painted colours plus the base, not every colour in the drawing.
sketch4.png is 503 x 629 px for a 119.813 x 150.065 unit drawing: 4.1982 px per unit across and 4.1915 down, a 0.16% disagreement that comes from the export, not from the art.
